_read: A small shop's cash register, documented the Holdrim way: the example to show someone who has
never seen the method. Four pages — why the till exists, the rules of a sale, closing the day,
and the contract with the supplier's system — every block approved by the owner. Then the shop
extended the return period from 7 to 14 days, and the owner approved the new sentence. Two
rules written on top of the old one turned red (🔴) without a letter of them changing — one on
another page. That red is the whole point: open the home and follow it.
bash engine/run-local.sh examples/cash-register      (from the repository root)
name: Cash register
